_meta.purpose: Per-check firing thresholds. THIS FILE IS THE KNOB - never tune a threshold by editing engine code.
who_reads_it: tilawah/engine/tolerances.py - applied on every live attempt
tools/calibrate.py - the same numbers are what the harness scores against
how_to_use: 1. Record N takes you certify as CORRECT, list them in calibration/manifest.csv
3. Read the 'would need' column - the threshold that silences every false positive
4. Edit 'checks' below, then re-run: py -3.13 tools/calibrate.py
Step 4 reuses the cached transcription, so it takes seconds, not minutes.

margin_semantics.duration: margin = |heard_count - expected_count| in QPS units (one unit ~= one harakah). Fires when margin >= min_delta.
margin_semantics.discrete: no gradient - the letter is either right or wrong. Only min_mean_prob can gate it.

_meta.min_mean_prob: Clip-level CTC confidence floor. 0.0 disables. This gates the WHOLE attempt's check, not one phoneme - a per-phoneme confidence is not exposed by the model wrapper yet.
_meta.calibration_status: UNCALIBRATED. Every min_delta is 1, which reproduces the pre-tolerance behaviour exactly (any deviation fires). Guessing thresholds before measuring would invent the number this file exists to discover.
_meta.see_also: tilawah/content/rules.json -> _meta.how_to_promote: a code may only move to status 'ship' once it has a measured false-positive rate on correct recitation from a verified reciter. That measurement is calibrate.py's output.

sifa_observed._note: OBSERVATION ONLY - no learner ever sees these. typed_diff compares phoneme strings and does not read the predicted sifat at all, so tafkheem / hams / shidda / jahr have no detector yet. calibrate.py still reports reference-vs-predicted sifa disagreement on certified-correct audio, because that disagreement rate is the evidence that decides whether such a detector is buildable AT ALL. Treat every number here as a false-positive rate for a detector that does not exist yet.
